notes.decision: Translated as the Coptic numeral 'fifty' (= Sahidic ⲧⲁⲓⲟⲩ for 50), not as qualitative of ⲧⲁⲓⲟ 'honor'. The arithmetic confirms: 50 men × 3 Sundays × 7 angels = 1050 (line 11: ⲣ̄ⲙⲏⲧ ⲛ̄ϣⲉ ⲧⲁⲓⲟⲩ = 1000+50). Line 6 ϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲛ̄ϣⲉ ⲧⲁⲓⲟⲩ = 350 = 50 × 7 angels per Sunday for all 50 men. The numerical reading makes the entire calculation coherent.

Rendered 'stood before me' from the Lycopolitan idiom: ⲡⲁⲙⲏⲧ = 'my midst, my presence' + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' The opening situates the disciples standing in Mani's presence as he describes their fasting practice.
Translated as 1sg perfect of ⲱϩⲉ 'stand, establish' = 'I have established/stood (in).' The speaker reflects on the good they have stood/established through the three Sundays of fasting.
Lycopolitan reflexive ⲧⲕⲧⲁⲓ̈ = ⲕⲧⲟⲓ 'turn myself' + ⲁⲛ 'again.' Marks the transition from joyful arithmetic to grief — the speaker turns from reckoning blessings to confessing trouble.
Standard Coptic ⲧⲱⲃϩ̄ 'pray, entreat, beseech' with 2sg.m suffix. Marks the petitionary core of the disciple's address to Mani.

The disciple asks to be released from the πατρωνία 'patronage' of gods and angels — the cosmic-protective relationship pertaining to his ecclesiastical office (cf. ⲡⲁⲧⲣⲱⲛⲓⲁ in accumulated vocabulary). Rendered 'patronage of the gods and the angels' to preserve the technical Manichaean register.
Read as ⲧⲏⲧⲉ 'sum, total, completion' (variant of ⲧⲏ 'totality'). Fits the arithmetical context where the speaker is computing the grand total of angels begotten.
